text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.5% today to $422.26, extending a sharp two-day rally that saw the stock jump nearly 8% from Monday's close. The immediate driver appears to be a significant widening in the spread between U.S. and world oil prices—crude is trading at $96.16 domestically but $113.96 globally, the widest gap in the data set. Refiners like Marathon profit when they can buy cheaper crude domestically and sell refined products into global markets; this spread environment is favorable for their margins.

The broader backdrop reinforces this dynamic: the G7's plan to release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over four months, while initially sounding bearish for fuel prices, actually underscores tight global supply and the premium refiners can command on exports. Combined with U.S. refineries running at 92.5% capacity and geopolitical tensions (Iran strikes, Houthi conflict) pushing world oil prices higher, refiners have real room to capture value on the gap between cheap domestic crude and expensive global fuel demand.
